h: Plan your splash and explore beyond the towers
p: The waterpark works brilliantly as part of a bigger resort trip. Many families pair it with a theme park day, saving the waterpark for an arrival afternoon or a more relaxed second day when everyone's legs are a bit tired from queuing. It also gives younger children a break from the big rides and lets them enjoy something pitched at their level.

Pack swimwear, towels, flip-flops and a change of warm clothes, especially if you're planning to use the outdoor pools. Goggles help younger swimmers, and a waterproof phone pouch is handy if you want photos. Lockers are available, so you can keep valuables safe while you splash about.

How long to allow? A few hours is about right for most families, giving everyone time to try the Master Blaster, float on the lazy river and have a play in the shallower areas. Book in advance where possible, as the waterpark can be busy at peak times, especially in the school holidays.

The Staffordshire countryside around Alton is lovely and well worth exploring. The ruins and Gothic architecture of the original Alton Towers estate are part of the history of the area, and the village of Alton itself is pretty, with Alton Castle perched on a rocky outcrop above the Churnet Valley.

For more to do nearby, the Churnet Valley Railway runs heritage trains through the valley, and Peak Wildlife Park near Leek is a fantastic day out for animal lovers. The Peak District is also within easy reach, so walkers can head out for fresh air and big views.
